Class QwenModel

java.lang.Object
smile.deep.layer.LayerBlock
smile.llm.model.qwen.QwenModel
All Implemented Interfaces:
Function<Tensor,Tensor>, Layer
public class QwenModel extends LayerBlock
Qwen3.5 hybrid text model: embeddings, hybrid blocks, final norm, LM head.

When constructed with a TensorShardSpec, attention / FFN / DeltaNet projections are locally sized for that TP rank. Embeddings and the LM head remain replicated (full vocab) on each rank in phase 1.

Construct on CPU, load weights, then call to(Device) to place parameters and the RoPE frequency table. Install the KV pool afterward via setKvCachePool(KvCachePool, boolean) when full-attention layers are present.

    • invalidateDecodeCudaGraphs

      public void invalidateDecodeCudaGraphs()
      Drops captured decode / prefetch CUDA graphs while keeping durable token/RoPE/logits buffers. Required after MTP window verify or KvCachePool.truncateTo(int, int), which rebuild FlashInfer CSR tensors that a captured graph may still reference (replay → illegal memory access).

    • forwardVerifyGraph

      public Tensor forwardVerifyGraph(Tensor tokens, int startPos)
      Uniform MTP window-verify forward (query length S = numDrafts + 1, every batch row sharing the same start position) with optional CUDA graph capture / replay.

      Stage 4 shadow-run: whenever VerifyCudaGraph.enabled(), every call runs eager through the new stable-buffer / graph-capturable kernel path (see AttentionContext dispatch in GatedAttention.forwardUniform), and bucket/warmup bookkeeping in verifyGraphSession runs for real against live traffic shapes — but VerifyCudaGraph.captureEnabled() is false until Stage 5, so beginCapture is never reached. This lets the existing eager forward(Tensor, int, boolean) path serve as the numeric go/no-go reference for the new kernel/buffer plumbing before Stage 5 adds the (separate) capture/replay risk.

      Parameters:
      tokens - token ids [B, S].
      startPos - cache start position (uniform across the batch).
      Returns:
      logits in float32 [B, S, V] (graph path returns persistent buffer).

    • forwardVerifyGraph

      public Tensor forwardVerifyGraph(Tensor tokens, int[] startPositions)
      Ragged form of forwardVerifyGraph(Tensor, int): the B rows (concurrent requests) may be at different absolute positions. One graph is captured per (batch, windowLen); per-row positions, RoPE rows, KV write slots and the page-table CSR are rewritten in place before each replay. Falls back to the eager path when graphs are unavailable.
      Parameters:
      tokens - token ids [B, S].
      startPositions - KV write position of each row's first window token.
      Returns:
      logits in float32 [B, S, V] (the graph path returns a persistent buffer).

    • forwardVerifyGraphCodeEager

      public Tensor forwardVerifyGraphCodeEager(Tensor tokens, int startPos)
      Diagnostic only: runs the exact code a verify CUDA graph captures (forwardVerifyGraphCore(Tensor, int[], Tensor, Tensor, Tensor) with the graph-mode stable buffers and FlashInfer verify kernel) eagerly, so replay output can be compared against identical kernels with no graph involved. Returns an owned copy of the float logits [B, S, V].
      Parameters:
      tokens - window token ids [B, S].
      startPos - cache start position.
      Returns:
      owned logits.

    • invalidateVerifyCudaGraphs

      public void invalidateVerifyCudaGraphs()
      Drops a captured verify CUDA graph while keeping durable token/RoPE/ logits buffers. Required after KvCachePool.truncateTo(int, int) rebuilds (not bumps-in-place) the FlashInfer CSR tensors a captured graph may still reference (replay → illegal memory access).

    • forwardBatchedVerify

      public Tensor forwardBatchedVerify(Tensor tokens, int[] startPositions, int[] cacheLengths)
      Batched eager verify forward for a cohort of concurrent requests that may be at different absolute positions — the multi-request counterpart of forwardVerifyGraph(Tensor, int), which requires a single shared start position across the batch so it can be CUDA-graph-captured (see VerifyCudaGraph#canGraphVerify). This always runs eager; heterogeneous-position batched cohorts do not graph-capture (a deliberately deferred fast-follow — see the batching plan).
      Parameters:
      tokens - token ids [B, windowLen].
      startPositions - KV write position of the window's first token per row.
      cacheLengths - inclusive cache length per row (prompt + already-sealed generation).
      Returns:
      logits [B, windowLen, V] in float32.
